{"thought":"The `prompt` function uses a nested `prompt_func` to handle the actual input. It seems to echo the prompt text and then calls `prompt_func` to get user input. The comment about backspace clearing the whole line indicates that this is a known issue. I will now create a test that simulates this behavior to confirm the bug. The test will use `click.prompt` to check if the backspace functionality behaves incorrectly on Linux. I will write a test file that will fail due to this bug.","final_test":"import click
import pytest

@pytest.mark.parametrize('input_text, expected_output', [
    ('a', 'a'),
    ('ab', 'ab'),
    ('abc', 'abc'),
])
def test_backspace_behavior(monkeypatch, input_text, expected_output):
    # Simulate user input with backspace
    user_input = input_text + '\b'  # Simulate backspace after input
    monkeypatch.setattr('sys.stdin.read', lambda: user_input)

    # Call the prompt function
    result = click.prompt('Enter text:', default='default')

    # Check if the result is as expected
    assert result == expected_output

# This test is expected to fail due to the backspace issue."}
